title: Factors influencing the process of learning mathematics among visually impaired and blind people
reason: Compares an alternative computer-aided maths teaching method with classical teaching using a psychologist-prepared questionnaire across seven factor categories (Wilcoxon, Cohen's d); no platform-recorded measure is related to success or a construct.

extraction.design: within-subject comparison of two teaching methods (questionnaire)
extraction.n_quote: The research group consisted of 71 blind or visually impaired stu-
extraction.population: blind/visually impaired students aged 19-24 in secondary school or first year of technical school, Silesia
extraction.outcome_or_construct: questionnaire ratings of behavioural, emotional, cognitive, social, distracting, motivational and modelling factors
extraction.notes: Population mixes secondary and technical-school students (E3 not clear-cut, not applied). Effect sizes are method comparisons on self-report categories.
